answer: Coordination-Density Pricing. Each identity's action rate is capped by the diversity of distinct counterparties it has transacted with in the prior window. A new identity enters through a narrow inlet: it can only interact with a small, randomly assigned set of peers, and every additional counterparty cluster it touches raises its required payment exponentially. The system treats a sudden broadening of counterparties as a signal of coordinated sybil expansion and throttles it. A separate crystal records each identity's interaction fingerprint, so paying more does not bypass the cap,
